portName: Santa Cruz Huatulco cruise pier (Bahía de Santa Cruz)
seoTitle: Huatulco cruise port guide: beaches, bays and Crucecita
seoDescription: Huatulco ships dock at Santa Cruz; the beach is 200 m away. Taxi to La Crucecita US$3–5, La Entrega 6–10 min. Mexico cruise fee US$10 from August 2026.
quickAnswer: Ships dock at the pier in Santa Cruz Bay, so there is no tender, and Santa Cruz beach and marina are a few minutes' walk from the gate. La Crucecita, the main town, is about 2 km away: a hot 20–30 minute walk or a US$3–5 taxi. Be back on board 60 minutes before all-aboard, and allow longer if you go out to a far bay by boat.
intro: Huatulco is a planned resort area spread along a string of bays on the Oaxaca coast, with much of the coastline inside a national park. The cruise pier is in Santa Cruz Bay, a small beach-and-marina district with restaurants and shops. The real town, La Crucecita, sits a short taxi ride inland with its plaza, church and market. The day here is about water: a swim at Santa Cruz, snorkelling at La Entrega, a boat trip along the bays, or the Zapotec site at Copalita. Calls are relatively few, so even a single ship can feel busy at the pier.

terminals.name: Santa Cruz Huatulco cruise pier
terminals.notes: Ships berth alongside in Santa Cruz Bay. Santa Cruz beach is immediately left of the pier gate (about 150–200 m) and the marina, where boat trips leave, is to the right (about 300–400 m). There is a tourist information desk in the terminal and taxis wait at the pier. No bank ATM at the pier; banks are in La Crucecita.

walkability.detail: Santa Cruz beach, the craft market and the marina are 2–7 minutes' walk. La Crucecita is about 2 km by a footpath that rises and falls and has little shade: 20–30 minutes, tiring in the heat. Most people walk Santa Cruz and take a taxi to La Crucecita.

transportSections.detail: Santa Cruz beach is directly left of the pier gate; the craft market and marina are a few minutes further.

transportSections.cost: About US$3–5 to La Crucecita; about US$5 Tangolunda; about US$6 El Maguey; about US$30 an hour (2026, per vehicle)
transportSections.time: 5–10 min to La Crucecita; 6–10 min La Entrega; 20–25 min Copalita
transportSections.detail: Taxis wait at the pier. They have no meters, so agree the fare before you get in, and confirm whether it is per car or per person. Pay cash, preferably pesos. Uber is not reliably available.
Leave the port, turn right on the main road, then left after about 100 m onto a wide footpath. It is not signed for La Crucecita, goes up and down, and has little shade.

Small boats from the marina reach bays such as San Agustín and Cacaluta that are hard or impossible to reach by road. Agree the price, the bay and an exact pick-up time before leaving. Missed pick-ups from remote bays have made passengers miss their ship.

returnTiming.rule: Be back on board 60 minutes before all-aboard. From La Crucecita, take a taxi back at least 75 minutes before; from Copalita, leave at least 90 minutes before.
returnTiming.detail: Re-boarding security takes 10–15 minutes and longer on multi-ship days. Boat trips to remote bays depend on the boatman coming back on time, so set the pick-up at least two hours before all-aboard. Independent operators are not waited for by the ship.
returnTiming.emergencyFallback: From La Crucecita, the taxi stand on the main plaza gets you to the pier in 5–10 minutes. If you are stuck at a remote bay or running late, call the port agent number on your daily programme straight away.

diyVsExcursion.item: Bays by catamaran plus La Crucecita
diyVsExcursion.diy: Taxi to La Crucecita about US$3–5 per car; boat trips from Santa Cruz marina negotiated locally
diyVsExcursion.saving: Not calculated; boat prices not verified

diyVsExcursion.ship: Varies by line; check your cruise planner
diyVsExcursion.diy: Taxi 20–25 min each way, fare agreed in advance

excursionAdvice: Santa Cruz beach, La Crucecita and La Entrega are cheap and easy without a tour. A ship's catamaran tour is worth it if you want to see several bays in one go without negotiating boats, and it returns you to the pier. Take a ship tour for anything far inland, such as waterfalls or coffee farms 1.5 hours or more away, where a delayed return is a real risk.

dayPlan.intro: Assumes the ship docks at 08:00 and all-aboard is 17:30.

steps.what: Off the ship. Pick up a map at the information desk in the terminal and agree a taxi fare to La Entrega.
Swim and snorkel in the sheltered bay before it gets busy. Rent gear on the beach.
Walk the plaza and the Parroquia de Nuestra Señora de Guadalupe (cover shoulders and knees). Lunch in La Crucecita.
Browse the market for alebrijes and embroidered clothing; use a bank ATM if you need pesos.
Taxi back to Santa Cruz, 5–10 minutes.
Last swim or drink at Santa Cruz beach beside the pier.
Back on board, 60 minutes before all-aboard.

sights.name: La Crucecita
sights.why: The main town, with a leafy central plaza, the area's best-value restaurants, banks and the market.
sights.tip: Take a taxi there in the heat and walk back only if you have time to spare.

sights.name: Parroquia de Nuestra Señora de Guadalupe
sights.why: La Crucecita's church on the main plaza.

sights.name: La Entrega
sights.why: Calm, sheltered bay with clear, shallow water, the easiest snorkelling near the pier.
sights.cost: Free entry; taxi fare and gear hire extra
sights.tip: Go early, before tour boats and groups arrive.

sights.name: Bocana del Río Copalita archaeological zone
sights.why: Zapotec temples and ceremonial plazas inside Copalita Eco Park, beyond Tangolunda, with a site museum.
sights.tip: Open daily 09:00–17:00 according to INAH. Bring water; little shade.

sights.name: Huatulco bays by boat
sights.why: Several bays, including Órgano, Maguey, San Agustín and Cacaluta, are best or only seen from the water, much of it inside Huatulco National Park.
sights.cost: Ship tour from US$84 (Holland America, 2026); private boats negotiated
sights.tip: Fix the return time in advance and keep the boatman's phone number.

sights.name: Santa Cruz beach and marina
sights.why: Small beach and marina right beside the pier, with restaurant-bars behind the sand.
sights.tip: The beach is small and partly taken by restaurant tables; good for a last swim before boarding.

sights.name: Tangolunda Bay
sights.why: The main resort bay with a viewpoint over the coast.
sights.tip: Combine with Copalita, which is further along the same road.

beaches.name: Playa Santa Cruz
beaches.howToGetThere: Walk left from the pier gate
beaches.note: Small and close to the pier; restaurant tables cover part of the sand.

beaches.name: La Entrega
beaches.cost: Free entry; taxi fare agreed in advance
beaches.note: Calm, clear water and the best easy snorkelling. Beach club with food and drink.

beaches.name: Bahía El Maguey
beaches.note: Bay with palapa restaurants on the beach.

beaches.name: Bahía Chahué
beaches.note: Beach clubs and the Bladu'Yú restaurant on Playa Principal.

food.dish: Pescado a la talla and seafood soup
food.where: El Grillo Marinero, Calle Carrizal, La Crucecita (closed Tuesdays)

food.dish: Mole negro and quesadillas with chapulines

commonMistakes.mistake: Walking to La Crucecita at midday.
commonMistakes.fix: The path has little shade and goes up and down. Take a US$3–5 taxi and save your energy.

commonMistakes.mistake: Taking a boat to a remote bay without a firm pick-up time.
commonMistakes.fix: Agree the price, the bay and the pick-up time before you leave, and set it at least two hours before all-aboard.

commonMistakes.mistake: Paying in dollars at pier-side stalls.
commonMistakes.fix: Ask for the peso price. Dollar prices and exchange rates are usually worse.

commonMistakes.mistake: Expecting a bank ATM at the pier.
commonMistakes.fix: Use bank ATMs (BBVA, Banamex, Santander) in La Crucecita; non-bank machines charge high fees.

commonMistakes.mistake: Getting into a taxi without agreeing the fare.
commonMistakes.fix: Taxis are unmetered. Agree the fare, and whether it is per car, before you set off.

safety: Huatulco is one of the tourist areas of Oaxaca that the US government lists as open to its staff without restriction; the state as a whole carries an 'exercise increased caution' advisory because of crime. Normal precautions apply: watch for pickpockets around the La Crucecita plaza on busy days, use taxis from the pier or the plaza rank, and leave valuables on the ship or in a locker at the beach. Ask at the terminal information desk about currents before swimming at open beaches, and use reef-safe sunscreen.
scams: Guides steering passengers to particular jewellery shops for commission. Compare silver prices in more than one shop before buying.
Unofficial guides and drivers outside the pier gate. Use the taxis at the pier and agree the fare first.
Inflated US dollar prices at pier-side stalls. Ask for the price in pesos.
accessibility: The pier has level walkways and Santa Cruz beach and marina are a short, flat walk. The footpath to La Crucecita is hilly and not suitable for wheelchairs; take a taxi. Ship catamaran tours need you to manage a few steps on and off the boat and coach, and Holland America marks its bays tour as not wheelchair accessible. INAH lists accessibility features at the Copalita site, but paths there are uneven.
rainyDay: The cruise season, November to April, is the dry season, so rain is unusual. If it does rain or the sea is rough, spend the day in La Crucecita: the church, the plaza cafés and the market. Boat trips may be cancelled in heavy swell.
crowdTips: Huatulco gets few calls compared with bigger Mexican ports, but a single ship fills Santa Cruz beach and La Entrega quickly. Go to La Entrega first thing and visit La Crucecita around midday. On days with two ships, leave the pier earlier and allow 20 minutes more for the return.

faqs.a: No. Ships dock at the pier in Santa Cruz Bay.

faqs.q: Is Huatulco walkable from the cruise port?
faqs.a: Santa Cruz beach and marina are 2–7 minutes away. La Crucecita is about 2 km, a hot 20–30 minute walk, so most people take a US$3–5 taxi.

faqs.q: How do I get from Huatulco cruise port to La Crucecita?
faqs.a: Taxi from the pier, 5–10 minutes and about US$3–5 per car. Agree the fare before you get in.
Santa Cruz beach is beside the pier. La Entrega, 6–10 minutes by taxi, is the best for snorkelling. El Maguey and Chahué are also short taxi rides.

faqs.q: What can I do in Huatulco in one day from a cruise ship?
faqs.a: Snorkel at La Entrega, see the plaza and church in La Crucecita, or take a boat along the bays. Copalita's Zapotec site is 20–25 minutes by taxi.

faqs.q: Do cruise passengers pay a fee to visit Mexico?
faqs.a: Yes. Mexico's cruise passenger fee rose to US$10 from 1 August 2026 and is due to reach US$15 from 1 July 2027. It is charged once per itinerary, usually through your cruise line's taxes and fees.

faqs.q: Do I need pesos in Huatulco?
faqs.a: Dollars are widely accepted, but pesos get better prices and are needed for taxis and small vendors. Bank ATMs are in La Crucecita.
Huatulco is a tourist area without US government travel restrictions, though Oaxaca state carries an increased-caution advisory. Watch for pickpockets on busy days.
